claim: RPD says experienced commanders mostly act on the first recognised option without comparing options. Primary abstract (2010 edit of the 1985 study): 26 commanders (mean 23 years of experience), 156 decision points, under 12% with simultaneous comparison of two or more options, over 80% direct identification of a typical situation and action. The '80-90%' figure is secondary; the share between 12% and 80% (up to about 8%) is not described in the abstract. Full report and postscript text still unread (HTTP 403). Coding is by the original authors.
agent_test: Measure how often the S0 first answer equals the answer after full deliberation, per task type, at equal tokens.

claim: The take-the-first rule (first generated option better than later ones) is supported in handball and basketball, but all numbers are second-hand (primary papers closed access, effect sizes unread). A rival long-term-working-memory model predicts the opposite sign and has support (nurses, soccer: later options better). A 2025 knowledge-free task (44 healthy, 53 MDD) found first options less unique than later ones, medians 122.7 vs 374.5 and 155.7 vs 542.0. No large independent replication found.
agent_test: Generate k options in order; compare quality of option 1 against the best of k on our task set.

claim: Prompting an LLM with a recognition-primed or data-frame frame raised triage accuracy over a plain prompt: 63.3% to 67.6% (RP) and 66.7% (DF); 10 ChatGPT models, 45 vignettes, 10 runs each. One study, one domain. The only control is a plain prompt: no chain-of-thought arm, no token comparison, and the authors say part of the gain may be extra reasoning.
agent_test: Run RP-style prompt vs plain vs plain chain-of-thought at equal tokens on several classification tasks; report per-class accuracy.

claim: The NDM prompt gain is concentrated in the hardest low-urgency class (self-care 13.4% to 29.8%) and looks like removing a default over-triage bias rather than better recognition.
agent_test: Compare confusion matrices with and without the frame to see whether the answer distribution just shifts.

claim: The NDM prompt gain is not uniform: larger in reasoning than non-reasoning models (OR 2.15) and absent in the newest family (GPT-5.2 Instant 57.8/56.4/55.3; Thinking 52.0/53.1/51.8).
agent_test: Test the frame on the strongest base model we use; expect no gain if the model already reasons well.

claim: Intuition is trustworthy only when the environment is regular and the person had prolonged practice with feedback; subjective confidence is not a valid signal of accuracy.
agent_test: Split tasks into regular-with-feedback vs irregular; measure S0 accuracy and confidence calibration on each. Full text of Kahneman & Klein not opened; Grove from memory.

claim: Speed costs accuracy even for elite experts: 20 grandmasters blundered more in blitz (0.20 to 0.27 proportion, d=1.39; expected blunder per move 0.20 to 0.38), so expertise is not recognition alone. Matches earlier Chabris & Hearst and Kasparov simultaneous-play findings.
agent_test: Cut the thinking budget on a task set and measure the error curve; test a router that spends more on hard cases against a flat budget.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: A familiar solution blocks a better one even in experts (Einstellung): Candidate Masters found the shorter mate 0% with the familiar line present, 100% without; eye data show they kept looking at the familiar line while saying they searched. Sheridan & Reingold extended it independently.
agent_test: Plant a familiar-but-suboptimal solution in a task set; measure S0 lock-in and whether a forced second-look operator escapes at equal tokens.

claim: Experts detect cues faster than novices (407 vs 719 ms to first fixation) but total dwell time does not differ; the expert edge is early detection, not longer search.
agent_test: No direct test; weak design input.

claim: Experts use a mix of RPD paths. One handball goalkeeper: simple match 46%, simulation 34%, diagnosis 20%; sport reviews report 60-81% simple matching, 13-28% diagnosis.
agent_test: Log which branch (answer, diagnose, simulate) our agent takes per task; do not borrow the sport base rate.

claim: Code review and ICU resident decisions are well described by an RPD-style orientation phase then an analytical phase; heuristics, premature closure and confirmation bias are the failure modes. Descriptive evidence only.
agent_test: Use as vocabulary, not as evidence of benefit.

claim: A fast default plus a slow module triggered by violated expectations beats single-system agents: SwiftSage 84.7 vs ReAct 36.4, Reflexion 45.3, fast-only 49.22 on ScienceWorld, at 757 vs 2,983 (Reflexion) tokens per action. DPT-Agent and Dualformer show the same pattern.
agent_test: Port the triggers (K zero-reward steps, invalid action, critical decision, surprise) into S0 and compare to always-slow at equal tokens.

claim: Execution-time validation helps a dual-process agent more than episodic memory: success 23.99% to 41.33% with a self-reflection checker vs 26.94% with memory.
agent_test: Add a cheap post-check to S0 and measure success and slow-call count.

claim: Reasoning models over-think easy items. First round already correct in over 92% of cases (QwQ-32B, R1 on ASDIV and MATH500 only); about 75% of AIME24 samples hold an early point where exit is correct; 60.8% of correct MATH-500 and 35.1% of correct GPQA samples stay correct at 20% of steps. Easy problems peak at about 1.5K thinking tokens, hardest at about 8K (R1-32B); past about 7K tokens flips turn net harmful. Confidence-threshold early exit (0.95) cut chains 19.1-80.1% with accuracy +0.3 to +5.0 (DEER); answer-repeat stopping cut over 40% of tokens on NQ but is unstable on hard sets.
agent_test: Measure how often our first answer is final-correct on easy items; test an early-exit rule at equal accuracy.

claim: Forcing a modern LLM to answer without chain of thought costs little on trap items (GPT-4 95% to 88% correct), and few examples build a fast pattern response (2% to 92% after 2 examples on one task): LLM intuition is trainable by exposure.
agent_test: Compare no-CoT vs CoT accuracy per task type on our model; add worked examples to the quick path.

claim: Pattern recognition alone can reach expert level when training covers the domain: a 270M transformer reaches Lichess blitz Elo 2895 with no search; ablations show it depends on data and scale.
agent_test: Ablate retrieved examples in S0 and watch accuracy on out-of-distribution items.

claim: LLMs degrade in dynamic environments: a fire-evacuation benchmark shows a drop of over 50% dynamic vs static; hierarchical prompts add up to 4.6%.
agent_test: Test whether our agent re-checks state when the task changes mid-run.

claim: Pre-mortem style prompts (list failure modes first) cut harm: InvThink harmfulness 3.22 to 2.19; the forecasting agent study credits pre-mortems for part of its gain. The link to NDM is by analogy only.
agent_test: Hand off to the premortem subfield; equal-token test of failure-mode listing vs extra sampling.

claim: Klein's argument that RPD is hidden from student labs because it needs 10-20 years of experience is untested for agents; lab critics (Lipshitz 2001, 16 commentaries) wanted controlled tests.
agent_test: Use fixed-task benchmarks as the control the critics asked for.

claim: NDM training tools (ShadowBox: Marines n=59, +28% expert alignment; CTA training g=0.871) have effects reported only second-hand with self-defined measures.
agent_test: Do not use as agent evidence.

claim: LLM agents in wargames escalate and ignore stated player traits, so persona text does not change fast-path behaviour.
agent_test: Vary persona text on the same decision task; expect no change.

claim: Grove et al. (2000) meta-analysis abstract confirmed: mechanical prediction about 10% more accurate than clinical on average; substantially better in 33-47% of studies and clinical substantially better in only 6-16%; the pattern held across task, judge type and judge experience. The '136 studies' count is still unverified. No LLM-judge versus formula test was found; one small 2026 comparison shows logistic regression 84.1% vs prompted LLMs 60-80% on 1,190 cardiac records (LLM test set about 30 cases).
agent_test: Give the agent a task with a scored formula; compare its quick judgment, its judgment plus the formula, and the formula alone.

claim: Early-exit rule for S0: stop at a reasoning boundary when a trial answer has confidence at or above about 0.95 (DEER), or when the answer repeats across checkpoints (works on easy tasks, unstable on hard). Allow longer thinking on hard items. A hidden-state probe saves 24% of tokens but needs weights access.
agent_test: Compare fixed-budget, answer-repeat and threshold stops at equal accuracy, split by difficulty.

claim: Escalation triggers tested for text-only agents: SwiftSage uses four hand-set triggers (5 steps of zero reward, invalid action, critical decision, unexpected observation) with no per-trigger ablation. ReflexGrad fires the slow process after 5 low-progress scores; m=3 over-triggers (84.3% vs 88.1% on GPT-5 ALFWorld, 5 calls per false activation), m=10 misses recoveries.
agent_test: Log trigger type and outcome; sweep the stall length 3, 5, 7.

claim: LLMs are fixated by misleading familiar structure: with red herrings removed, GPT-4 0-shot rose from 6 to about 59 solved walls (OnlyConnect, 2023), but a six-item mental-set test gave noisy, mixed results. No measured penalty size and no forced re-look test for LLM agents was found.
agent_test: Build a familiar-but-worse option task; compare with and without a forced second look.

claim: A model's stated confidence moves its behaviour but tracks competence poorly: inserted confidence or doubt sentences swung delegation by a median 20.6 points (53-70 on larger models) yet well-targeted flips beat chance by only +2 points. A 2026 judge study finds verbalized confidence useful on newest proprietary models, so this may be model-dependent.
agent_test: Check on our model whether stated confidence predicts correctness per task regularity.

claim: LLMs show a working-memory-like load limit: retrieval of the latest value falls log-linearly with interference (PI-LLM); N-back accuracy falls with load in 15 models up to 14B, with the limit in readout under interference. No direct LLM test of a 3-variable, 6-transition cap exists.
agent_test: Vary variables and transitions in a simulate task to find our model's break point.

claim: Reasoning models form a quick internal guess before reasoning; when later reasoning conflicts with it they overthink. Removing the question text after the first step cut reasoning length 31.1-53.5%.
agent_test: Log first guess vs final answer; measure extra tokens when they differ.
